The most successful application of benefit evaluation in our case studies was for the purposes of project selection and communication with stakeholders, not cost allocation. Regions have multiple pathways to update their cost allocation methods, but the process remains complex and requires stakeholder engagement. The report also highlights the processes by which regions can update their cost allocation methods, including through compliance filing to federal regulations and exercising filing rights from Sections 205 and 206 of the Federal Power Act. As the summary highlights, implementing changes is not simple because each region has split authority among multiple stakeholder groups to file cost allocation changes. This report focuses on the seven U.S. grid operators, either regional transmission organizations or independent system operators.
